reviews.text:
I visited Dynamic Maze while looking for something to do in Insa-dong!
I chose it because it is an indoor experiential space so you can play regardless of the weather.

The location was not difficult to find as it was on the main street of Insa-dong, and since it is indoors, it would be perfect for a hot or rainy day.

When you enter, there is a space where you can take off your shoes and experience it, so it's a good idea to wear comfortable clothes. I went wearing sneakers, but I ended up sweating a lot while working out. There are more sections where I use my body than I thought.

It is in the form of a maze, and there are elements such as obstacles and missions in between, so it is not a simple maze.
It's not a completely difficult level, but my friend and I were like, "Huh? What is this?" It's fun to solve it while doing it.

In particular, it was more fun because we moved together as a team, and there were a lot of laugh points because it required subtle cooperation.
There were also points where you could take pictures, so it was nice to make memories along the way.

reviews.author: jangwon choi
reviews.text:
This week, I visited the Central Methodist Church in Jongno-gu.
This church was especially recommended by my father and is located on top of a building in Insa-dong, Jongno-gu.
Jungang Church was originally founded by Henry Appenzeller in 1890 and was called Jongro Church at that time.
Appenzeller led the Christian enlightenment movement based at the Central Methodist Church.
In 1901, Jongno Girls' Elementary School and Religious Church Kindergarten were established.
In 1918, Chung-Ang School was opened to train kindergarten teachers. This was the predecessor of Chung-Ang University. In 1930, the name was changed from Jongno Church to Chung-Ang Church.
After moving to Insa-dong in 1975, Hanaro Building was built in 1983.
In 1999, Hanaro Central Church in Paju was opened as the 100th Anniversary Church, and Dream Church near Sungshin Women's University in Seongbuk-gu was opened as a separate church.

Jungang Church is located on the 11th floor of Hanaro Building, next to Jongno Police Station in Seoul.
Originally, the church was intended to be built on top of the building, so there is a large worship space.
The 12th floor is a children's banquet space, and part of the 10th floor is a space for infants and kindergarteners.
There is a small chapel on the first basement floor where early morning worship is held.

Sunday services include the first part of the service at 9 o'clock and the second part of the traditional service at 11 o'clock.
The event will be hosted by the associate pastor, and the sermon will be delivered by the senior pastor, Pastor Hyungno Lee.
Pastor Hyungno Lee served as an associate pastor at Jeongdong First Church.
He came as senior pastor of Central Church in 2017.

Impression 1.
I went in on time for the 11 o'clock service and attended the service right away.
Because it is a traditional worship service, the general order is hymns, litany, doxology, representative prayer,
In particular, after the representative prayer, we pray together with the Lord's Prayer.
After consecration, hymn of consecration, prayer of consecration, Bible reading, praise from the choir,
Lastly, it continues with the senior pastor’s sermon. A concise order of worship.

Impression 2.
Central Church is also an old church, and the main worship floor appears to be people in their 60s or older.
It appears that about 150 people will attend the second service.
Most of the people are elderly, so it feels subdued rather than lively.
That's why the church motto was 'Fill my house'.
It appears that they want to fill the church again.

Impression 3.
The second part of the praise group is the Messiah Praise Band, and the number of people appears to be about 20 people.
I heard there were one male and one female soloist.
It was a little disappointing that there wasn't much of a sense of the overall sound coming together.
Most of the praise band members also appear to be in their 40s or older.
The ensemble consists of 6-7 people, mainly string instruments, and everyone feels like professionals.

Impression 4.
I liked Pastor Hyungno Lee’s sermon.
As he calmly tells the story, all of this is according to the title of the grace of the Lord.
I got the feeling that he spoke well of illustrations and theology.
When I saw that you came from Jeongdong First Church to Jungang Church,
I feel like I have taken an elite course.

Impression 5.
The atmosphere of the church itself was quiet and calm.
As soon as the service is over, everyone seems to go home or enjoy a love feast.
When we told them we had visited, they didn't show much interest in us, so we just had a leisurely service and moved to Insa-dong.
There is a marker indicating that this is the central point of Seoul selected by the Korean Empire.
So, it is assumed that the name of the church was changed from Jongro Church to Jungang Church.

reviews.author: jangwon choi
reviews.text:
On the 18th, Hannam Church belonging to the Presbyterian Church of Korea in Seongdong-gu was visited.
On the 25th, we visited Chodong Church belonging to the Presbyterian Church of Korea in Jongno-gu.

Chodong Church was founded on August 15, 1945, with the liberation of the motherland, and Pastors Kim Jong-dae and Yoo Jae-gi of the Gyeongseong Herbal Orthodox Church, where the Japanese used to worship, took over the church and brought in Pastor Ham Tae-young. Chodong Church of the Presbyterian Church of Korea was founded, and received approval for establishment from the Gyeonggi Presbytery in October.
After 1945, Baekbeom Kim Gu sometimes attended worship services.
After the Korean War, a tent church was built, a board church was built in 1955, and a brick church was built in 1959.
In October 1972, a new church was built and relocated to Donui-dong, Jongno-gu, with one underground floor and six floors above ground. In 2010, the church underwent major repairs, and Cafe Grazie opened on commission on the first floor.

Chodong Church's Sunday services are held at 8 a.m. and 11 a.m., and the afternoon service is at 2 p.m. It is located in an easy-to-find location where you can take Exit 3 or Exit 2-1 of Jongno 3-ga Station.
The church building has a chapel on the 6th floor and a restaurant on the 5th floor. It is a 50-year-old building, but major repairs were completed in 2010, so the church is maintained in neat condition.

Impression 1.
The service begins with an organ accompaniment, and after the entrance song and the choir's main music, the call to worship, a silent confession of sin, a common prayer, and the Lord's Prayer are sung together, then a litany is read. After the pastor's pastoral prayer, the Bible is read, and after a special praise from the choir, the senior pastor gives a sermon. It begins with the senior pastor's entrance, followed by a confession of sin, a word of forgiveness, a litany, and the confession of the Apostles' Creed, followed by a representative prayer by the elder. At the end, we prayed the Lord's Prayer again and then the pastor gave a sermon. After the sermon, there is a consecration prayer, and after the sending song, it ends with a blessing prayer.

Impression 2.
The current senior pastor, Pastor Seongho Son, was appointed as the 6th pastor in 2012. He received a Master of Divinity from Hanshin University Graduate School and a Master of Theology from the University of Geneva, Switzerland. He was appointed as an associate pastor at Chodong Church in 2007, and then moved to Seoul East Presbytery Milal Church as a senior pastor. The overall impression of the pastor was friendly and the sermon was good, but I felt a little sleepy.

Impression 3.
The second part of the Hosanna Choir consists of about 30 people and appears to be conducted by Deacon Jae-yeon Son, who was appointed in 2018. It sounded like each part had a soloist, and overall it was an acceptable praise.

Impression 4.
There were signs of people coming together under the slogan for 2024, which is to fill our homes with one mind, but it was disappointing that there didn't seem to be many people attending the service overall.
It was disappointing that there didn't seem to be many young people compared to the size of the church.
However, during the week, a restaurant called Chodong Bibim is opened and serves meals to 20 to 30 people. It is said that you can eat bibimbap if you make a reservation through Naver Reservation. It would be a good idea to donate around 3,000 won.

Impression 5.
It was my first time going there and I arrived a little late, so I had a hard time walking up the stairs without knowing that the chapel was on the 5th floor. So I guess everyone is in front of the elevator. The stained glass in front of the chapel was pretty, and the LED cross on the left wall was also pretty. The church site was small, so the chapel was not spacious, but it was cozy.

I thought this place was really cool. It seemed like a place where individuals could set up their own stalls and sell whatever they wanted. I didn't talk to all the sellers, but I looked around. Among them, I met a really kind and gentle seller. Although he spoke English quite well, he seemed to have difficulty conveying ideas and information. I felt like he was trying to better convey what he wanted to say by using Google Translator. I could feel that he was sincerely trying to communicate in English. I'm not sure exactly what area he was in, but when we were there, he was under the signs that said rooms 107 and 106. I'll attach a photo. We bought a few things from him. He knew what gifts it was traditional to give which items to which people in Korea, and he also made recommendations on what gifts to buy for my family.

If she happens to read this, thank you so much again! I wish her all the best for her future and thank you for all your help.

reviews.author: T channel
reviews.text:
A must-visit tourist course if you visit Insa-dong.
There are a variety of small workshops and shops that can only be seen here.

The square-shaped building has a spiral-shaped movement path, so if you look around slowly, you will reach a height where you can look down on Insa-dong.

The building itself is unique, but the store layout is also nice, so stop by on your way to Gyeongbokgung Palace or Bukchon Hanok Village.

Please note that the restroom is open to the public for convenient use, and a flea market is often held on the first floor.

reviews.author: Jiyoung Lee
reviews.text:
2025.10
It's been a while since I went to a place I really like.
A famous spot with a lot of cool stores!! Traditional craft shopping mall 
A street of art filled with the scent of tradition, including calligraphy and antiques, it is a landmark in Insa-dong. There are more than 70 stores in the four-story building, and since opening in 2004, it has become a famous spot in Insa-dong as a place where you can not only shop, but also go on a food tour and appreciate art.

The entire building, which is filled with traditional Korean crafts, unique miscellaneous goods, and props and accessories that are perfect as gifts, is a unique structure that can be called art, and can be enjoyed just by looking around.

If you come to Insadong, be sure to stop by.

There are still a lot of couples, families, and tourists, and there are a lot of things to see, so it's a place worth visiting.

Of course, there are franchise prop shops such as Kakao, but if you come here because you want to shop in a street like Hongdae, you will probably find it boring.
